rows.title: CT’s wealth inequality remains a looming obstacle to tolling cars
rows.standfirst: While many issues killed Gov. Ned Lamont’s plan to toll passenger cars, fears about the impact it would have on the poor weighed heavily on some lawmakers.

rows.title: Dems and GOP share common flaws in transportation plans
rows.standfirst: Democrats and Republicans don’t want to acknowledge that their plans share two common weaknesses — economic risk and a lean rebuilding program.

rows.title: Action unlikely on transportation, local aid until January
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont suggested Tuesday that long-delayed state grants to municipalities would be delivered by Christmas. That is unlikely to happen.

rows.title: Wooden hopes divestiture of gun stocks sparks a national trend
rows.standfirst: State Treasurer Shawn Wooden brought his “Responsible Gun Policy” tour to Washington D.C. Wednesday to try to persuade other states to follow his lead.

rows.title: For Democrats and labor, tolls are a family fight
rows.standfirst: Democrats say settling on a transportation financing plan is key to the state’s economic growth. It also is important to their relationship with labor.

rows.title: Hospitals to receive $1.8 B to settle provider tax lawsuit against CT
rows.standfirst: Connecticut hospitals will receive $1.8 billion in state and federal funds between now and 2026 to resolve a lawsuit that could have cost the state as much as $4 billion, according to details released Thursday by Gov. Ned Lamont.

rows.title: Union agency paying back money missing from Sandy Hook Workers Fund
rows.standfirst: A state audit requested by a Republican lawmaker revealed that funds meant to support workers present at the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting were not used appropriately.

rows.title: Lamont: Average truck tolls of $8 could buy $19.4B in improvements
rows.standfirst: Truck tolls face a certain legal challenge, but they could finance $19.4 billion in infrastructure improvements over 10 years.

rows.title: Connecticut’s legacy of debt weighed heavy on Lamont’s first budget
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont had lofty goals, but found was that fixing Connecticut’s budget meant grappling with the state’s enormous debt.

rows.title: CT lawmakers hail U.S. House approval of prescription drug bill
rows.standfirst: The most controversial section of the bill would direct the secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services to directly negotiate with drugmakers on the price of medications covered under Medicare.

rows.title: How they came to a $1.8 billion hospital settlement
rows.standfirst: Hospital executives and the Lamont administration pulled back the curtain Friday on a proposed $1.8 billion settlement with Connecticut’s hospitals.

rows.title: Education partnership discusses budget, hires and plans — all in open session
rows.standfirst: That’s a contrast to the first meeting, which was conducted mostly behind closed doors. The partnership has been criticized for a lack of transparency because it originally planned to hold all its meetings privately.

rows.title: If cautiously, Lamont exploring health care reform
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration is part of a working group exploring health care reforms for 2020. He was late to the debate in the last session.

rows.title: Some holiday cheating on Lamont’s ‘debt diet’
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont loosened the tight grip he’s kept on borrowing as the state Bond Commission met Wednesday for only the fourth time in 2019.

rows.title: Legislature approves hospital settlement and restaurant law
rows.standfirst: The General Assembly unanimously voted in special session Wednesday to accept the settlement of a high-stakes lawsuit in which the hospital industry claimed billions in damages from a complex taxing scheme.

rows.title: Education partnership seeks public input, issues request for information
rows.standfirst: The group released a Request for Information Friday to learn more about programs that already exist in the community and needs that are not being met.

rows.title: Best of 2019: Lamont’s pension shift would leave CT’s children deep in debt
rows.standfirst: Faced with another huge deficit, Lamont and Democratic lawmakers are weighing whether to shift billions of dollars in pension debt onto the next generation of taxpayers.

rows.title: Best of 2019: Partisan battle heats up over whether new CT budget is balanced
rows.standfirst: Republican leaders argue it is unbalanced and unconstitutional, relying on labor savings still to be negotiated.

rows.title: Best of 2019: So you think you know about transportation and tolls?
rows.standfirst: Tolls, gas taxes, highways, bridges and rail lines are in the news. How much do you know about them?

rows.title: Best of 2019: Debunking Connecticut’s enduring tax myth
rows.standfirst: There’s an oft-told tale about the income tax. And it’s completely false.

rows.title: Best of 2019: Lamont: Trust me. GOP lawmakers: Why should we?
rows.standfirst: As Gov. Lamont tries to convince lawmakers that tolls will remain fixed, his history is working against him.

rows.title: Best of 2019: Nonprofits say philanthropy alone can’t save services
rows.standfirst: Frustration with Gov. Ned Lamont, who won’t give struggling nonprofits money from the state $2.5 billion reserve, surged after he urged them to ask more from wealthy donors.
